answer: A reputation bridge between an agent's verified work history and its right to transact stops cheap sybil swarms. Think of each agent as an island: it earns trust only by completing paid, checkable tasks over time, and a small saffron-colored stake is locked per identity, slashed on fraud. An attacker spinning up thousands of islands must fund every stake and redo months of honest work for each one, so the cost of faking a crowd exceeds any reward the crowd could extract.
